newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION - NATAL/NORTHERNS CURRIE CUP FINAL FAVOURED.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - NATAL/NORTHERNS CURRIE CUP FINAL FAVOURED.

text.p: The smart money has been on a Natal versus Northern Transvaal Currie Cup final since the end of this year's Super 12 encounters and Saturday's two semi-final matches should produce this result.

The Natal Sharks and the Blue Bulls were South Africa's best provinces by some distance in the Southern Hemisphere Super 12 championship, with Natal impressively putting out Queensland before losing to powerful Auckland in the final.

Natal, the defending Currie Cup champions, are unbeaten in this season's competition and their clash with Free State at Kings Park on Saturday will feature the two most expansive, running sides in South African domestic rugby.
Although Natal will be without their hard-running Springbok flyhalf Henry Honiball (hamstring niggle), they have envied strength in depth and are expected to win at home with some comfort.
The Durban-based side have been head and shoulders above all their opponents this year in terms of ball handling, ball retention and flowing interplay between forwards and backs.
Crucially, Free State will be missing the services of two of their key tight forwards in lock Ryno Opperman and loosehead prop Os du Randt - both out through injury.
The pair failed fitness tests on Tuesday night, Opperman because of a knee injury and du Randt with an injured coccyx.

But Natal coach Ian McIntosh is not taking Free State lightly as a result: "That's a great loss for them, as I rate both players highly. Os du Randt is an outstanding player and Ryno Opperman is regarded as one of the best jumpers in South Africa. But I know Free State and they will have adequate replacements on Saturday.
"Free State are always a very dangerous side - and they've proved that. They'll break from anywhere and, next thing, you've got a try behind your poles.

"Yet our players are well aware what's at stake and it's going to be very hard to take it away from them...I know that. They're very determined and they want to see themselves get through," McIntosh told Reuters.
In the other semi-final, Northern Transvaal entertain Transvaal at Loftus Versfeld where a tough forward battle can be expected for at least the first half.

Transvaal's Golden Lions are beginning to display some sort of form after several sketchy performances this year and their deposed Springbok captain Francois Pienaar is bound to breathe fire both into himself and his team.

Transvaal field the same line-up which knocked out Western Province in the quarters while Northerns once again prefer the relative inexperience of tighthead prop Willie Enslin to Springbok incumbent Marius Hurter.
If they are to be any suprise packages in this weekend's semi-finals, Loftus is the more likely venue of the two.
